SMTO-SKL-0142 — SMTO couldn't find the file to send to Slack

GUID: 1882aaa8-658f-535a-992d-287cb8557b87
Slug: slack-artifact-reference-invalid
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: slack

What happened

  • The file you asked SMTO to send to Slack doesn't exist anymore, belongs to a different conversation, or couldn't be opened. Nothing was sent to Slack.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Make sure the file was made or attached in this conversation, not in a different one. If it came from elsewhere, attach it here first. SMTO only sends files that belong to the conversation asking for them.
  2. If the file was in this conversation's workspace, check that it's still there and hasn't been renamed, moved or deleted. SMTO looks the file up by its saved location, so a moved or deleted file can't be opened.
  3. Ask the Agent to upload the file again, naming it clearly so it picks the right one. A fresh request lets the Agent choose a file that SMTO can actually find.

What success looks like

  • The Agent reports the upload finished and the file appears once in the Slack channel.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Files saved elsewhere on the computer can't be sent directly; attach them to the conversation first.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Slack upload was refused because the source_ref is not an artifact://, art_ or artifact-workspace:// reference that resolves to an artifact owned by this conversation (resolution raised ValueError or OSError).

What this means

  • Artifact source resolution raises a ValueError or OSError for the selected reference or workspace source. The diagnostic performs no Slack request. Inspect the original receipt and operation stage to determine effects; keep workspace, principal and exact channel/message identities fixed during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • Artifact source resolution raises a ValueError or OSError for the selected reference or workspace source.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect exact reference, ownership, materialization and safe underlying failure.

How to fix it

  • files.source accepts only artifact://, art_ or artifact-workspace:// references and opens them through ArtifactStore.open_stream with the current conversation_id. Confirm the artifact exists and is owned by this conversation (or that the workspace path registers successfully), then pass that exact reference; arbitrary host paths are rejected.
  • Use an existing conversation-owned artifact:// or artifact-workspace:// source reference.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect exact provider state and authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended supported artifact reference resolves and passes integrity checks.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • The diagnostic performs no Slack request. Inspect the original receipt and operation stage to determine effects; keep workspace, principal and exact channel/message identities fixed during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
